answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a slashable bond before it may vote on a task: for example, a fixed deposit locked in a public contract and forfeited if the agent signs conflicting attestations. Splitting one operator into a thousand names then requires funding a thousand bonds, while detectable equivocation burns them; the bond is an anchor, not proof of unique personhood. A relic credential or wharf address alone cannot bypass the deposit, so the attacker pays capital and risks losing it.
